title: Learning, memory and other cognitive processes
summary: Applying learning theories in education, the reliability of memory, biological, cultural and environmental influences on cognition, and ways to improve memory.

keyterms.definition: A system using tokens as reinforcers that can be exchanged for rewards, based on operant conditioning.
Information after an event that can distort memory of it, e.g. leading questions.
A witness's account of an event, which may be distorted by schemas, questions or stress.
Recall is better when the environment at recall matches that at learning.
Practising retrieval improves long-term retention more than restudying.
Spreading study out over time leads to better long-term memory than cramming.
Failing to notice an unexpected stimulus when attention is focused elsewhere.
How cultural practices such as schooling influence cognitive strategies.

questions.prompt: In Loftus and Palmer (1974), participants who heard the verb "smashed" estimated speeds that were:
options: The same as all other verbs
questions.explanation: The wording of a leading question affected estimates, and later more people falsely recalled broken glass.

questions.prompt: Yuille and Cutshall (1986) interviewed real witnesses to a shooting months later. They found:
options: Witnesses were quite accurate and resisted misleading questions
questions.explanation: This challenges the ecological validity of lab studies like Loftus and Palmer.

questions.statement: Godden and Baddeley (1975) found divers recalled words better when learning and recall happened in the same environment.
questions.explanation: Matching land–land or underwater–underwater improved recall, showing context-dependent memory.

questions.statement: Simons and Chabris (1999) found that nearly all participants noticed a person in a gorilla suit while counting passes.
questions.explanation: About half failed to notice, showing inattentional blindness.

questions.text: Better recall when the learning and recall environments match is called ___-dependent memory.
questions.explanation: Environmental cues help retrieval.

questions.text: Cole and Scribner (1974) found Kpelle people with formal ___ were more likely to use categorical clustering in recall.
questions.explanation: Memory strategies depend on cultural practices such as schooling.

questions.prompt: Match each influence on memory to a study.
questions.explanation: Cognition is influenced by biological, cultural and environmental factors.

questions.prompt: A limitation of Loftus and Palmer (1974) is that:
options: Students watching film clips lacked the emotion of real events
questions.explanation: Low ecological validity: watching a clip is not witnessing a real accident.

questions.prompt: Which finding links attention and technology use?
options: Drivers on phones may miss unexpected hazards, like participants missing the gorilla
Inattentional blindness only occurs at night
questions.explanation: Limited attention means unattended events may not be perceived.

questions.prompt: Order the procedure of Loftus and Palmer's first experiment.
items: Participants watch film clips of car accidents
They answer questions about the clips
The critical question uses one of five verbs
Speed estimates are compared across verb groups
questions.explanation: Only the verb differed between groups (IV).

questions.prompt: Roediger and Karpicke (2006) compared restudying with practice testing. After a week:
questions.explanation: Retrieval practice strengthens long-term memory: the testing effect.

questions.prompt: A teacher gives points for good behaviour that students can exchange for privileges. This is:
questions.explanation: Token economies apply operant conditioning in classrooms.

questions.statement: Spacing study sessions over several days usually leads to better long-term memory than cramming.
questions.explanation: Cepeda et al. (2006) found strong support for the spacing effect in a meta-analysis.

questions.statement: Restudying notes feels easy, so it is always the most effective revision strategy.
questions.explanation: Feeling familiar is not the same as learning; retrieval practice is more effective.

questions.text: Improving recall by practising retrieval is called the ___ effect.
questions.explanation: Self-quizzing is retrieval practice.

questions.text: Spreading study over time rather than cramming makes use of the ___ effect.
questions.explanation: Spaced practice gives repeated chances to retrieve and consolidate.

questions.prompt: Match each learning strategy to its theory.
questions.explanation: Educational practice draws on several approaches.

questions.prompt: A criticism of token economies is that:
options: Behaviour may stop when tokens are removed, and they may reduce intrinsic motivation
They are based on schema theory
They are only used with animals
questions.explanation: Extrinsic rewards may not generalize outside the system.

questions.prompt: Darley and Gross (1983) found that viewers rated "Hannah's" ability differently depending on:
options: Whether she appeared to come from a high or low socioeconomic background
questions.explanation: Schemas about class biased judgements of the same performance, a confirmation bias.

questions.prompt: Order a revision plan using evidence-based strategies.
questions.explanation: Combining testing with spacing maximises retention.
